newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia wheat forecast reduced to 310,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Georgia wheat forecast reduced to 310,000 tonnes.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Georgia expects a 1997 wheat crop of around 310,000 tonnes, down from previous forecasts of 400,000, an official from the Agriculture and Food Ministry said late on Thursday.

Deputy Minister Simon Uzunashvili forecast output at 300,000-320,000 tonnes, far above the 179,000 harvested in 1996 but less than the 400,000 tonnes predicted earlier this year. The 1995 harvest was just 125,000 tonnes.
He said the reduced forecast was due to scattered rainfall and late frosts.
"From the beginning, the situation was good, because seeds and fertilizer were brought to sowing areas in time," he said. "But late frosts and spring hail were a bad influence on the harvest."
Georgia consumed 1.2 million tonnes of wheat a year in the 1980s, but annual consumption had fallen to 600,000 tonnes per year by 1994/95.
Georgia imported over 300,000 tonnes of wheat last year, mostly in the form of humanitarian aid and shipments from other ex-Soviet republics.
The country no longer levies value added tax and customs duties on wheat imports.
